brief.topic: Teardown: what one AI chat session tells you without a rating
brief.audience: PMs choosing feedback metrics for AI features
constraints: Session log is illustrative and labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Ratings are rare, but regenerations, heavy edits, copy-outs and abandonment show where AI answers worked or failed, so log them from day one.

hooks.text: Nobody clicks thumbs-down. Read what they do.
The user rewrote 70% of the answer. Rating: none.
hooks.notes: Vivid but needs an illustrative label on frame 0.

hooks.text: Your feedback button is mostly silent.
hooks.notes: True but doesn't promise a fix.

selectionRationale: Highest total (22/25): relatable, credible, and the reel shows exactly which behaviours to log.

scenes.onScreen: LOG FROM DAY ONE / Track what users do. / Regenerate: the first answer missed · Heavy edits: right idea, wrong words · Copy or send: the answer got used · Abandon mid-task: it failed or was too slow / Ratings tell you why. Behaviour tells you where to look.

caption.opening: Most AI answers never get a rating. They still leave a trail.
body: In the (illustrative) session in this reel: regenerated twice, 70% of the text edited, then copied out. No thumbs either way.

Log these from day one:
→ Regenerate: the first answer missed
→ Heavy edits: right idea, wrong words
→ Copy or send: the answer got used
→ Abandon mid-task: it failed or was too slow
Ratings tell you why. Behaviour tells you where to look.

claims.text: Implicit behavioural signals (regenerations, edits, copy-outs, abandonment) are more plentiful than explicit ratings and help locate AI answer failures.
Session log: 2 regenerations, 70% edited, copied out, no rating.

repurposing.followUpReel: Format 3 (A vs B): thumbs-up rate vs task success (already queued as q020; follow with edit-distance as a metric).
